title: Customer request funnel + prioritization rubric for Private/VPC/on-prem asks (networking, upgrades, air-gapped)
creator: Lina Chen
description:
Problem statement:

We are receiving an increasing volume of ad-hoc customer asks for Private/VPC/on-prem deployments that touch three recurring constraint areas: networking (proxy/fw/NAT/egress policies), upgrade compatibility and orchestration for on-prem customers, and strict air-gapped deployment requirements. Currently requests are handled inconsistently across AE/SE/PM which creates long response latency, missed expectations, and lack of signal to prioritize engineering work.

Goal:

Define a lightweight but actionable request funnel (intake -> discovery -> scoring -> decision) and a prioritization rubric focused on the private deployment constraints above so we consistently: 1) respond to customers within SLA for first-touch and estimated delivery, 2) capture standard technical constraints and deliverable templates for engineering prescreens, and 3) produce a ranked backlog that balances strategic deals, engineering cost, and cross-customer reusability.

Outcomes / Acceptance criteria:

- A documented intake form/template instrument (used by AE/SE/Support) that captures minimal reproducible environment details for networking, upgrade cadence, and air-gap constraints.
- A prioritization rubric with scoring fields: customer strategic value, security/compliance risk, reusability, engineering complexity estimate, and time-to-value.
- Decision gates defined (Triage/Discovery/Engineering Review/Design & Schedule) with SLA targets: first response 3 business days, discovery completion 10 business days, engineering scoping 20 business days.
- Example mapping of 8 recent historical requests into the rubric to validate scoring distribution and thresholds.
- Templates/PRD skeletons for common outcomes: VPC peering + CNI adjustments, private upgrade runbook, air-gapped installer checklist.
- Owner and rotation schedule for intake reviews (weekly intake meetings).

Proposed approach:

1) Run a 2-week discovery with SEs and Support to collect 12 representative request records and capture missing fields we need in the intake form.
2) Draft a scoring rubric and threshold guide; simulate on the collected records and iterate.
3) Build a short Google Form + Notion intake template and a triage spreadsheet that computes scores automatically.
4) Pilot the funnel for 4 weeks with one AE team and one customer success pod.
5) Surface outcomes to Eng leadership and solicit commitment levels for P0/P1 work that affects core runtime or install artifacts.

Stakeholders:

- PM lead: Lina Chen (creator)
- SE lead: Diego Ramos (assignee)
- Support: Priya Nair
- Engineering liaison: Marco Alvarez (Runtime)
- Security/compliance: Emily Stone

Notes & trade-offs:

- We must avoid over-bureaucratizing intake. The form should be intentionally minimal and the scoring transparent.
- Some requests (large enterprise deals) will require fast-track exceptions; the rubric should capture 'escalation reason' and require executive sign-off.
- For air-gapped installs, engineering effort can vary widely; include a fallback option to engage Professional Services for custom work and track revenue offsets.

Risks:

- If engineering do not commit to SLOs for scoping response, customers will still see latency. Mitigate by documenting what engineering will and won't scope in the first pass.
- Mis-scoring could skew backlog toward low-reuse large deals. Mitigate by weighting reusability higher for non-strategic customers.

Next steps (owner & timeline):

- Week 1 (owner: Diego): Kickoff discovery and compile 12 sample requests (due 2025-02-25).
- Week 2 (owner: Lina): Draft intake form and scoring rubric; review with SE/Support (due 2025-03-04).
- Week 3 (owner: Diego + Marco): Map rubric to engineering scoping definitions and tag any runtime blockers (due 2025-03-11).
- Week 4 (owner: Lina): Pilot intake with AE pod and collect feedback (due 2025-03-18).

Artifacts / links:

- Triage spreadsheet: [link to shared sheet] (placeholder)
- Example requests archive: drive:/private-deploy-requests/2025-Q1 (placeholder)

Open questions for leadership:

- What SLA commitment can Eng leadership provide for scoping private deployment requests?
- Should we require a minimum ARR or contract threshold to consider exceptions to the scoring rubric?
- Do we route all air-gapped work through a Professional Services offering or allow Eng to accept project work?
